penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Remediating Salesforce permission configurations and middleware architecture requires hands-on, org-specific technical work per customer — not automatable by Claude prompts alone.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Enterprise security and compliance engagements with IT/security teams invariably require scoping calls, discovery sessions, and sign-off meetings.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Each org's integration mix (Docusign, etc.) differs; ongoing support requires human judgement calls as integrations update.

rationale: The buyer is a real, identifiable business role (Salesforce admin / IT security lead at a mid-market company) facing a genuine compliance deadline — willingness to pay is plausible. However, the solution requires per-org technical work: auditing permissions, reconfiguring integrations, and potentially building middleware proxy layers — none of which can be delivered as an automated Claude prompt. Both `operational_autonomy` (3) and `buildability_with_ai` (3) are well below build-gate floors, and three human-touch penalties push the total to 2.0. This is a consulting engagement, not a scalable micro-service.
solution_plan: This opportunity is NOT viable for a solo non-technical operator running an autonomous Claude factory. The core deliverable — least-privilege permission remediation or an integration proxy layer for a specific Salesforce org — requires org-specific Salesforce configuration expertise, hands-on API work, and bespoke security architecture decisions per client. There is no version of this that Claude can build once and deliver automatically to many customers. If Youval had deep Salesforce admin expertise and wanted to do consulting, this could be a paid engagement — but that is the opposite of the factory model. Drop and do not pursue.
notes: Failing build gates: operational_autonomy (3 < 7), buildability_with_ai (3 < 6). Even ignoring penalties, weighted_total of 5.0 is below the 5.5 validate threshold.
